    Credit Graph

    Who controls whom, who issued what, and how each debenture's spread compares to that of comparable peers. 1,244 series from 383 issuers in 31 segments, updated every business day with public data from ANBIMA, SND, CVM and ANEEL.

        Control and risk map

        Click a segment, then a risk group and a company. The profile opens alongside; click an issue to see the security.

        How to read the map

        Each large bubble is a segment; within it, each bubble is a risk group, sized by the number of series. The color of the bubbles, groups, and issuers is the macro-sector; the color of each issuance is the spread deviation relative to peers. Opening a company shows the issuances and documents (material facts, indentures, news, and analyses); click a document to open the original. Click the group name to collapse. Dotted lines between bubbles indicate companies shared between groups. Drag to move and use the mouse wheel or two fingers to zoom in.

        Found a bond? The sheet next to it leads to the simulation and the peers. To compare the entire segment, go to Relative Value →

        Relative value

        Observed spread minus the fair spread of peers, already with the event adjustment. On the right, the series spread is above the fair value estimated by peers; on the left, below. Click a bar to open the profile.

        How it's calculated

        Fair spread = median of the 8 most comparable series from other issuers, in the same segment, same class (IPCA+ or DI+), and same band (main or high yield). Color marks the size of the deviation in standard deviations of the residuals. Deviation is not a recommendation: part of it is a liquidity premium the model does not measure.

        below peers above peersSite-wide, red = higher spread or rate (lower price) and blue = lower.

        Curve and spread simulator

        Combine a yield curve shock with a credit spread shock and see the effect on price. The two add up in the security's rate; the price responds to the sum, with a small cross-term from convexity.

        How it's calculated

        IPCA+: the real cash flow from the SND schedule is discounted again at the indicative rate plus the shock in the real interest rate curve (NTN-B) plus the shock in the spread. DI+: cash flow projected by the ANBIMA prefixed curve and discounted at (1 + DI) × (1 + spread). A parallel shift in the DI curve changes the projected interest and the discount by the same amount, and the effect on price is negligible; that is why the curve shock is disabled in DI+.

        Glossary of indicators

        The same explanation appears in the "i" button next to each number on the site.

        Rules

        • Payment flow from the SND event schedule; validated against ANBIMA duration. Series that don't match are excluded and shown flagged.
        • Comparable spread: Z-spread over the real zero-coupon curve (ETTJ IPCA, ANBIMA), with a gross-up of 15% on the nominal rate of incentivized debentures (tax-exempt for individuals), using the inflation implied in each series' duration.
        • High yield band: IPCA+ series with market Z-spread ≥ 300 bps, DI+ with spread ≥ 300 bps over CDI, or issuer with a negative credit event (JEV, confidence ≥ 0.8) in the last 12 months. Excluded from the regression and only compared against other high yield series.
        • Comparable peers: mandatory filters for same segment, same class (IPCA+ or DI+) and same band (main or high yield; high yield with fewer than 3 peers in the segment compares across segments); among candidates from other issuers, the 8 closest by structure (project finance or corporate), asset phase (construction, transition, operational; rule based on concession age at ANEEL, refined by JEV), sponsor, guarantee, tax exemption, duration, headroom until end of concession, and size. Explicit weights in analises/pares.py. The fair spread is the median of the peers.
        • Event adjustment (provisional, conservative): negative credit +25 bps, other negative impact +8, operational advance −5, only with JEV confidence classification ≥ 0.8; half-life of 60 days, window of 180, caps by type (−10 / +20 / +40) and of ±40 per issuer. It will be recalibrated through an event study once history is available.
        • Fair spread from the regression (second reading): provisional model using duration, real collateral, controller declared to CVM, issue size and dispersion of ANBIMA contributions. Deviation is not a recommendation: part of it is a liquidity premium the model doesn't capture.
        • DI+: the ANBIMA indicative rate is already the spread over CDI; deviation against the median DI+ of the pilot (small sample).
        • Historical change: difference between today's spread and the first day of collected history (since Sep 24, 2026). Gains meaning over time.
        • Risk group: "CVM" = legal-entity controller declared in the Reference Form; "indenture" = shareholder, guarantor or intervening party named in the indenture's preamble (read and subject to review); "inferred" = explicit rule, pending confirmation. Issuer identified by SND's CNPJ.
        • Documents: only title, date, source and link, from public sources (CVM IPE, trustees, Google News and public pages of research firms). Content stays at the original source. Analyses filtered by credit terms (debenture, rating, debt, earnings).
        • Event classification (JEV): the System One model by TypeSafe reads the title of each material fact, announcement, notice, news item and analysis and returns event type, impact on the creditor and relevance, with confidence. Validation on 50 documents (Oct 2, 2026): 89% accuracy on event type when confidence is ≥ 0.8 and 36% below that; only the first group is shown as classified, the rest appears "to review". Titles with no content are not submitted. The impact criterion follows the JEV's (on-time payment, fundraising and matured auction tend to be positive) and is under calibration.
        • Clauses ("Indenture" column): presence of guarantee, fiduciary assignment, cross-default and net debt/EBITDA covenant, located by text rules in public indentures (Pentágono and CVM IPE). Evidence to review, not a legal reading.
